summary: Enhanced analysis mode in Business Central (2026 release wave 1): developers can package analysis views in AL apps via exported JSON files, page extensions and profile customizations. Also covers view descriptions as tooltips, read-only shipped views, and built-in views announced for 28.x.
overview:
The video explains why analysis mode is getting further investment and demos how to ship analysis views from AL apps. The workflow is to set up a view in Business Central, export it as JSON, and reference that file from a page extension or source page using the definition file property.

The demo then shows the result in a deployed environment. Shipped views appear read-only with a locked icon, users can duplicate them to get editable copies, and users can hide views through personalization. The presenter also announces built-in analysis views for sales, finance, inventory and purchasing pages, coming in 28.x.
key_points: Analysis views can be exported from Business Central as JSON files and packaged in AL apps through page extensions or source pages.
Page extensions use a definition file property that points to the exported JSON file.
Views can also be added to page customizations and profile extensions, so they are available only to users with specific roles.
Views shipped in an app are read-only and show a locked icon; the filter pane is removed, and users can duplicate a view to edit the copy.
Descriptions set through the rename action in analysis mode show as tooltips and override the JSON settings.
Users can hide views they do not need through personalization mode.
Built-in analysis views are announced for 28.x, including sales orders, change log entries, user lists, GL register, fixed asset ledgers and item ledger entries.
